title: Mushroom Patty Stir-Fried Rice
subtitle: with Broccoli and Carrot
description: Mushroom patties add a ‘meaty’ texture and umami flavour to this healthy, fibre-rich brown rice stir-fry. With heaps of carrot and broccoli, this certainly ticks lots of good-for-you boxes.

steps.text: Cook rice: Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Cook three-quarters of the rice (see Kitchen notes) for 25 mins or until tender. Drain, then return to the pan and cover to keep warm.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, peel the carrots, quarter lengthwise, then thinly slice. Trim the broccoli, then finely chop. Thinly slice the onion. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Put the kecap manis, 2 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp white vinegar, ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper and 1½ tbs water in a bowl and stir to combine.

Cook omelette: Put 1 egg in a bowl and whisk to combine. Spray or brush a large frypan with olive oil and heat over medium-high heat. Add the egg mixture and swirl to coat the base of the pan. Cook for 2-3 mins until set, then loosely roll up the omelette in the pan. Transfer to a board, cool slightly, then cut into thin strips. Reserve the pan.

Warm patties: Spray or brush the same pan with olive oil and heat over medium-high heat. Cook the mushroom patties (see Kitchen notes) for 2-3 mins each side until warmed through. Remove from the pan. Spray or brush the pan with olive oil again. Stir-fry the carrot, broccoli, onion and garlic for 3 mins or until tender but still with crunch.

Finish and serve up: Add the rice to the pan and stir-fry for 1 min. Add the sauce and stir-fry for a further 1-2 mins until the veggies and rice are completely coated and the sauce is absorbed. Slice the mushroom patties. Divide the stir-fry and patties among bowls. Top with the omelette strips and enjoy.

Kitchen notes: We have only used three-quarters of the rice to keep within our healthy eating guidelines, but it would be equally delicious if you decided to use it all. ~ Instead of frying the mushroom patties whole, you could roughly crumble them into the rice in step 5 and stir-fry them together.
